title: 2026 Semiconductor Capital Expenditure Outlook: Foundries Bet on Advanced Packaging
author: Daniel Okoro
content_text: Global semiconductor capital expenditure is forecast to reach $215 billion in 2026, a 12% increase over 2025, with the fastest-growing category being advanced packaging rather than leading-edge lithography. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Samsung Foundry, and Intel Foundry Services collectively earmarked more than $40 billion for chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) and hybrid-bonding capacity, the packaging techniques that stitch multiple dies into a single AI accelerator. Demand from AI training clusters is the primary driver: a single high-end accelerator now integrates a logic die, multiple high-bandwidth memory stacks, and an interposer, all of which depend on packaging throughput rather than transistor density. Analysts note that packaging capacity, not wafer starts, has become the binding constraint on accelerator supply through at least 2027. Memory makers SK Hynix and Micron are expanding high-bandwidth memory output in parallel, though yield on twelve-high HBM stacks remains below 70%. On the equipment side, lithography leader ASML guided to record bookings, but the report emphasizes that deposition, etch, and metrology suppliers tied to packaging, including Applied Materials and BE Semiconductor, are growing faster off a smaller base. Geographically, the report highlights the U.S. CHIPS Act and the European Chips Act as accelerating domestic packaging investment, reducing but not eliminating the concentration of advanced packaging in Taiwan. Risk factors include a potential AI-spending correction, export-control expansion affecting China-bound tools, and the capital intensity of hybrid bonding, which requires cleanroom precision approaching that of front-end fabrication.
